title: Tracker integrity prints record text to the job log, where the runner parses it as workflow commands (OPAG-971)
description: Reported by opum-agent as OPAG-971 (CI hygiene), 2026-09-30. The Tracker integrity workflow ran `bun run src/cli/main.ts task list --json` unredirected in its "Tracker reads cleanly" step, printing every record field to the job log. The Actions runner parses log lines that begin with workflow-command syntax, so record text controls the log: lore-cli measured this class at 846233e1, where a green job carried a failure-level annotation because a record note quoted a CI log line starting with the error-command prefix; the same mechanism covers add-mask and stop-commands. Record notes legitimately quote log excerpts, so this is an injection surface and an accidental-annotation generator at once. Fix: redirect the listing under $RUNNER_TEMP and print only a count, mirroring the fix landed in opum-ai/opum-agent#1662; the exit code keeps gating and the count is the positive control.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The Tracker integrity job prints no record text to its log: the task-list step writes the listing under $RUNNER_TEMP and prints a count line, verified by reading the green run log.

With a record carrying text the runner would parse as a workflow command (a line beginning with the error-command prefix), the job runs green with 0 annotations on the check run; the pre-fix behavior of the same text is on record from lore-cli 846233e1.
An empty or malformed listing fails the step rather than reading as zero records (the jq count gates).

plan: 1. Redirect the task-list step under $RUNNER_TEMP and print a count as the positive control, with a comment naming the workflow-command parsing reason.
2. Verify on the PR: green job, 0 annotations, count line in the log.
3. Negative control on the branch: plant a record note containing workflow-command text, confirm 0 annotations, then revert the plant before merge.
4. PR, required contexts green, squash-merge to dev; reply to opum-agent with the PR.
